header.title: Sentence fixer: capital letter and full stop
header.goal: Children fix scrambled sentences with a capital and a full stop.
header.subject: English

moves.do: Recall oo: the class spells good and moon together.
moves.how: Spell good and moon: g-oo-d, m-oo-n.
moves.say: “Which two letters make oo?” → “o and o.”

moves.do: Show p.143: the parrot and “the ball kicked Jojo”.
moves.how: Ask: “Where at home do you see a sentence?”
moves.say: “The parrot scrambled it. I can put words in order.”

moves.do: Fix “the ball kicked Jojo”; capital J, full stop, read.
moves.think: Who did the action? Jojo, so Jojo is first. Then kicked, then the ball. I write a big J and a dot. I read it and stop.

moves.do: Write “went The far ball”; class says the fixed sentence.
moves.how: Who is it about? The ball. Add capital T and a dot.
moves.say: “The ball went far.” → class stops at the dot.

moves.do: Window side fixes “Pinky cricket played”, other “football Jojo played”
moves.how: Controlled practice: write your fixed sentence; partner checks capital and dot on the board.
moves.say: “Who did the action? Say that word first.”

turn.a: Mine: “Pinky played cricket.” Capital and dot?
turn.b: (Ticks P and the dot.) Yes. Mine: “Jojo played football.”
turn.help: Point to the capital J; say “begin”.

moves.do: Fix the sentences alone in your book; read one aloud.
moves.how: 1. goal the into went It · 2. cheered Everyone · 3. pick the right one. Done? Why “ball kicked Jojo” fails.

sections.mistake: “jojo kicked the ball”. Ask: “Which letter is big? Why the dot?”
sections.stuck: Point to capital J, say “begin”; the dot, “stop”; write in chunks.

moves.do: Fix “won Pinky the trophy”: capital, dot. Read it.
moves.how: Who did the action? Start there. Read it, stop at the dot.
moves.say: “Which letter is big? Which dot ends it?”

sections.correct: Pinky won the trophy. Capital P, full stop, stops at the dot.
sections.success: I can fix a sentence: capital and full stop.
sections.ask: How did you know Pinky comes first?
sections.listen: Pinky did the action. A capital starts it, a full stop ends it.

moves.do: Family dictates “Jojo kicked the ball.”; write it once.
moves.how: Circle capital J and the full stop; read, stop at the dot.

expect.html:
GRADE 1 · ENGLISH · Ch.11 Game Day at Taleemabad!Day 4 · 40 min

Sentence fixer: capital letter and full stop

Children fix scrambled sentences with a capital and a full stop.
Bringtextbook pp.143-144 · chalk · books, pencils Wordssentence · capital letter · full stop Video📺 Capital Letter, Full Stop, Question Mark | Grammar For Kids | Periwinkle
PRACTICE · 24 of 40 min
5′ 8′ 12′ 12′ 3′
OpenExplainWe DoYou Do✓
★ Your one thing today · in move

Opening

0–5′Full details ›
1

Recall oo: the class spells good and moon together. Spell good and moon: g-oo-d, m-oo-n. “Which two letters make oo?” → “o and o.”

2

Show p.143: the parrot and “the ball kicked Jojo”. Ask: “Where at home do you see a sentence?” “The parrot scrambled it. I can put words in order.”

Explanation · I Do

5–13′Full details ›
3

Fix “the ball kicked Jojo”; capital J, full stop, read. Write it. “Jojo kicked the ball.”Think aloud: “Who did the action? Jojo, so Jojo is first. Then kicked, then the ball. I write a big J and a dot. I read it and stop.”

We Do

13–25′Full details ›
4

I START, YOU FINISH
Write “went The far ball”; class says the fixed sentence. Who is it about? The ball. Add capital T and a dot. “The ball went far.” → class stops at the dot.

5

ONE NEIGHBOUR TURN
Window side fixes “Pinky cricket played”, other “football Jojo played” Controlled practice: write your fixed sentence; partner checks capital and dot on the board. “Who did the action? Say that word first.”Window side first: “Mine: “Pinky played cricket.” Capital and dot?” → Reply: “(Ticks P and the dot.) Yes. Mine: “Jojo played football.”” · Stop: one clap, eyes on me · Stuck? Point to the capital J; say “begin”.

You Do · in the book

25–37′Full details ›
6

⏱ 25′ stop explaining
Fix the sentences alone in your book; read one aloud. 1. goal the into went It · 2. cheered Everyone · 3. pick the right one. Done? Why “ball kicked Jojo” fails. “Who did the action? Start there.”If stuck: Point to capital J, say “begin”; the dot, “stop”; write in chunks.

Check 5 books · answers

1.It went into the goal.
2.Everyone cheered.
3.C) Pinky played cricket.

Likely mistake

“jojo kicked the ball”. Ask: “Which letter is big? Why the dot?”

THE BOARD BY THE END · Scrambled, fixed, then capital and dot

Check · exit ticket

37–40′Full details ›
7

Fix “won Pinky the trophy”: capital, dot. Read it. Who did the action? Start there. Read it, stop at the dot. “Which letter is big? Which dot ends it?”Ask: “How did you know Pinky comes first?” → Listen for: Pinky did the action. A capital starts it, a full stop ends it.Success: “I can fix a sentence: capital and full stop.” 👍 or ✊ firstCorrect: Pinky won the trophy. Capital P, full stop, stops at the dot.

Homework

at homeFull details ›
8

Family dictates “Jojo kicked the ball.”; write it once. Circle capital J and the full stop; read, stop at the dot. “Jojo kicked the ball.”

Full lesson plan ›
